records.source: וַתְּהִ֨י צַעֲקַ֥ת הָעָ֛ם וּנְשֵׁיהֶ֖ם גְּדוֹלָ֑ה אֶל־אֲחֵיהֶ֖ם הַיְּהוּדִֽים׃
records.gloss: And was [the] outcry of the people and their wives great against their brothers the Jews.
pieces: Now the common people and their wives raised a great outcry against their fellow Jews.

L.1: And there was a great outcry of the people and their wives against their brothers, the Jews.

R.1: Some of the people and their wives began to complain loudly about other Jews.

decisions.choice: outcry: a cry for help against injustice
decisions.reason: The word is used of the cry of the oppressed that reaches God (Exodus 3:7, 9; Genesis 18:20-21). The people are not merely grumbling; they are crying out against wrong done to them.

decisions.choice: against their brothers the Jews: the wrong came from inside the community
decisions.reason: While enemies threatened from outside (chapter 4), the poorer families were being pressed by their own wealthier countrymen (verse 7). "Brothers" means fellow members of the people.

decisions.choice: and their wives: the women joined the complaint
decisions.reason: The wives are named because the debts touched whole households, and their sons and daughters were being taken (verse 5).

decisions.choice: fellow Jews (Balanced); other Jews (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "their brothers" means here (m2).

records.heading: The outcry of the poor against their own people

records.source: וְיֵשׁ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֹמְרִ֔ים בָּנֵ֥ינוּ וּבְנֹתֵ֖ינוּ אֲנַ֣חְנוּ רַבִּ֑ים וְנִקְחָ֥ה דָגָ֖ן וְנֹאכְלָ֥ה וְנִחְיֶֽה׃
records.gloss: And there were who were saying, our sons and our daughters, we [are] many; and let us get grain and let us eat and live.
pieces: Some were saying, "We and our sons and daughters are many. We must get grain so that we can eat and stay alive."

L.2: And there were [some] who were saying, "Our sons and our daughters, we are many. Let us get grain, so that we may eat and live."

R.2: Some said, "We have big families. We need grain so we can eat and stay alive."

decisions.choice: our sons and our daughters, we are many
alternatives: we are giving our sons and daughters as security
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "our sons and our daughters, we are many": large families need much food. A change of one letter would give "our sons and our daughters we are pledging", matching the mortgaged fields in verse 3 and the children forced into service in verse 5. The text as it stands makes good sense and is kept.

decisions.choice: let us get grain, that we may eat and live: a plea for food
decisions.reason: The verbs express a wish or need. The first complaint is simple hunger: the families are too large for what they have.

decisions.choice: We have big families
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "our sons and our daughters, we are many" means.

records.source: וְיֵשׁ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֹמְרִ֔ים שְׂדֹתֵ֛ינוּ וּכְרָמֵ֥ינוּ וּבָתֵּ֖ינוּ אֲנַ֣חְנוּ עֹרְבִ֑ים וְנִקְחָ֥ה דָגָ֖ן בָּרָעָֽב׃
records.gloss: And there were who were saying, our fields and our vineyards and our houses we [are] mortgaging, and let us get grain in the famine.
pieces: Others were saying, "We are mortgaging our fields, our vineyards and our houses to get grain during the famine."

L.3: And there were [some] who were saying, "We are mortgaging our fields and our vineyards and our houses, so that we may get grain in the famine."

R.3: Others said, "We have to give our fields, vineyards and houses as security for loans. That is the only way we can get grain during the famine."

decisions.choice: mortgaging: pledging property as security for a debt
decisions.reason: The verb means to stand surety or give something in pledge (Genesis 43:9; Proverbs 6:1). If the debt was not paid, the land passed to the lender (verse 5).

decisions.choice: the famine: a time of food shortage
decisions.reason: The text does not say what caused it. The building work also took men from their fields (4:16).

decisions.choice: give ... as security for loans; That is the only way
decisions.reason: Readable explains what mortgaging means and why they did it.

records.source: וְיֵשׁ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֹמְרִ֔ים לָוִ֥ינוּ כֶ֖סֶף לְמִדַּ֣ת הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ שְׂדֹתֵ֖ינוּ וּכְרָמֵֽינוּ׃
records.gloss: And there were who were saying, we have borrowed money for [the] tribute of the king [on] our fields and our vineyards.
pieces: Still others said, "We have borrowed money against our fields and vineyards to pay the king's tax.

L.4: And there were [some] who were saying, "We have borrowed money for the king's tax [on] our fields and our vineyards.

R.4: Still others said, "We had to borrow money to pay the king's tax on our fields and vineyards.

decisions.choice: the king's tax: the tribute paid to the Persian king
decisions.reason: The word is the tribute owed to the king of Persia, the same word used in the Aramaic of Ezra 4:13, 20. Land was taxed, so families borrowed against their fields to pay it.

decisions.choice: our fields and our vineyards: what the tax was on, or what the loan was secured on
decisions.reason: The two nouns stand at the end with no linking word. They name the land that was taxed, which also served as security for the loan.

records.source: וְעַתָּ֗ה כִּבְשַׂ֤ר אַחֵ֨ינוּ֙ בְּשָׂרֵ֔נוּ כִּבְנֵיהֶ֖ם בָּנֵ֑ינוּ וְהִנֵּ֣ה אֲנַ֣חְנוּ כֹ֠בְשִׁים אֶת־בָּנֵ֨ינוּ וְאֶת־בְּנֹתֵ֜ינוּ לַעֲבָדִ֗ים וְיֵ֨שׁ מִבְּנֹתֵ֤ינוּ נִכְבָּשׁוֹת֙ וְאֵ֣ין לְאֵ֣ל יָדֵ֔נוּ וּשְׂדֹתֵ֥ינוּ וּכְרָמֵ֖ינוּ לַאֲחֵרִֽים׃
records.gloss: And now like [the] flesh of our brothers [is] our flesh, like their sons [are] our sons; and see, we [are] subduing our sons and our daughters to [be] slaves, and there are [some] of our daughters subdued, and there is not [any] power [in] our hand, and our fields and our vineyards [belong] to others.
pieces: Our bodies are the same as those of our fellow Jews, and our children are just like theirs. Yet we are forcing our sons and daughters into slavery. Some of our daughters have already been taken as slaves, and we are powerless, because our fields and vineyards now belong to others."

L.5: And now our flesh is like the flesh of our brothers; our children are like their children. And look, we are forcing our sons and our daughters to be slaves, and some of our daughters have already been forced, and it is not in the power of our hand, and our fields and our vineyards belong to others."

R.5: We are the same people as our fellow Jews, and our children are as good as theirs. But we have to sell our sons and daughters as slaves. Some of our daughters are already slaves. We cannot do anything about it, because other people now own our fields and vineyards."

decisions.choice: our flesh is like the flesh of our brothers: we are their own kin
decisions.reason: "Flesh" means body and also kinship (Genesis 29:14; 37:27). The poor remind the rich that they are one family, so their children are worth no less.

decisions.choice: forcing our children to be slaves: debt slavery
decisions.reason: A family that could not repay a loan could have its children taken into service by the creditor until the debt was worked off (2 Kings 4:1). The law allowed a fellow Israelite to be held as a hired worker and freed in the seventh year or the jubilee, and forbade treating him harshly (Exodus 21:2; Leviticus 25:39-43).

decisions.choice: some of our daughters have been forced: perhaps with a hint of sexual abuse
decisions.reason: The verb means to subdue or force. Used of daughters, it may suggest that some were taken as concubines or abused (Esther 7:8 uses the same verb of assaulting a woman); the text does not say more.

decisions.choice: there is no power in our hand: we are helpless
decisions.reason: "It is in the power of my hand" means "I am able" (Genesis 31:29; Deuteronomy 28:32). With their land gone, they have no means to buy their children back.

decisions.choice: slaves, slavery
decisions.reason: The project usually renders this word "servant" at Balanced and Readable, but here people are being handed over as property for debt, so "slave" stays at every level.

records.source: וַיִּ֥חַר לִ֖י מְאֹ֑ד כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר שָׁמַ֨עְתִּי֙ אֶת־זַֽעֲקָתָ֔ם וְאֵ֖ת הַדְּבָרִ֥ים הָאֵֽלֶּה׃
records.gloss: And it burned to me greatly when I heard their outcry and these words.
pieces: I was very angry when I heard their outcry and these complaints.

L.6: And [anger] burned in me greatly when I heard their outcry and these words.

R.6: When I heard their complaints and what they said, I was very angry.

decisions.choice: it burned to me: I was angry
decisions.reason: The usual Hebrew idiom for anger, as in 4:1 of the enemies. Now Nehemiah's anger is turned on his own people's leaders.

decisions.choice: their outcry: the same cry of injustice as verse 1
decisions.reason: The word links back to the outcry of verse 1.

records.source: וַיִּמָּלֵ֨ךְ לִבִּ֜י עָלַ֗י וָאָרִ֨יבָה֙ אֶת־הַחֹרִ֣ים וְאֶת־הַסְּגָנִ֔ים וָאֹמְרָ֣ה לָהֶ֔ם מַשָּׁ֥אאִישׁ־בְּאָחִ֖יו אַתֶּ֣ם נֹשִׁ֑יםוָאֶתֵּ֥ן עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם קְהִלָּ֥ה גְדוֹלָֽה׃
records.gloss: And took counsel my heart upon me, and I contended with the nobles and with the officials, and I said to them, usury each on his brother you [are] lending; and I set against them a great assembly.
pieces: After thinking it over, I brought charges against the nobles and the officials. I told them, "You are charging your own fellow Jews interest!" Then I called a great assembly to deal with them.

L.7: And my heart took counsel within me, and I contended with the nobles and with the officials, and I said to them, "You are lending at interest, each against his brother." And I set a great assembly against them.

R.7: I thought about it carefully. Then I accused the leaders and the officials. I said to them, "You are making your own people pay you interest on loans!" So I called a large meeting to deal with them.

decisions.choice: my heart took counsel within me: I thought it over
decisions.reason: Nehemiah did not act in the first heat of anger (verse 6) but considered what to do.

decisions.choice: contended: brought a charge against
decisions.reason: The verb means to quarrel or to bring a legal case (Nehemiah 13:11, 17, 25; Isaiah 1:17). He accuses the leaders openly.

decisions.choice: lending at interest: making loans that bore interest or required pledges
decisions.reason: The noun refers to a loan made on terms that burdened the borrower, with interest or with the borrower's goods or children as security. The law forbade charging interest to a poor fellow Israelite (Exodus 22:24; Leviticus 25:35-37; Deuteronomy 23:20-21).

decisions.choice: a great assembly against them: a public hearing
decisions.reason: Nehemiah brought the matter before the whole community, so that the wrong could be judged and put right in public.

decisions.choice: nobles, officials (Literal, Balanced); leaders, officials (Readable)
decisions.reason: The book-wide terms for these two groups (2:16).

records.source: וָאֹמְרָ֣ה לָהֶ֗ם אֲנַ֣חְנוּ קָ֠נִינוּ אֶת־אַחֵ֨ינוּ הַיְּהוּדִ֜ים הַנִּמְכָּרִ֤ים לַגּוֹיִם֙ כְּדֵ֣י בָ֔נוּ וְגַם־אַתֶּ֛ם תִּמְכְּר֥וּ אֶת־אֲחֵיכֶ֖ם וְנִמְכְּרוּ־לָ֑נוּ וַֽיַּחֲרִ֔ישׁוּ וְלֹ֥א מָצְא֖וּ דָּבָֽר׃ס
records.gloss: And I said to them, we have bought back our brothers the Jews who were sold to the nations according to [the] means in us, and also you sell your brothers, and they will be sold to us! And they were silent and not they found a word.
pieces: I said to them, "As far as we were able, we have bought back our fellow Jews who had been sold to foreigners. And now you are selling your own fellow Jews, only for them to be sold back to us!" They kept silent and could find nothing to say.

L.8: And I said to them, "We, according to [the] means in us, have bought back our brothers the Jews who had been sold to the nations; and you, you are even selling your brothers, so that they may be sold to us!" And they were silent and could not find a word.

R.8: I told them, "We have done all we could to buy back our fellow Jews who were sold to foreigners. Now you are selling your own people, and we will have to buy them back again!" They had nothing to say.

decisions.choice: bought back: redeemed Jews sold as slaves to foreigners
decisions.reason: Nehemiah and others had paid to free Jews who had been sold to other peoples. The law gave relatives the duty to buy back a kinsman who sold himself to a foreigner (Leviticus 25:47-49).

decisions.choice: you are selling ... and they will be sold to us: a bitter contrast
decisions.reason: The nobles' debt-claims force poor Jews into slavery, so that others must pay again to free them. The question is rhetorical and points out the waste and the wrong.

decisions.choice: according to the means in us: as far as we could
decisions.reason: The phrase means "as much as was in our power".

decisions.choice: foreigners
decisions.reason: "The nations" are other peoples; Balanced and Readable say "foreigners".

records.source: וָאוֹמַ֕רלֹא־ט֥וֹב הַדָּבָ֖ר אֲשֶׁר־אַתֶּ֣ם עֹשִׂ֑ים הֲל֞וֹא בְּיִרְאַ֤ת אֱלֹהֵ֨ינוּ֙ תֵּלֵ֔כוּ מֵחֶרְפַּ֖ת הַגּוֹיִ֥ם אוֹיְבֵֽינוּ׃
records.gloss: And I said, not good [is] the thing which you [are] doing; [is it] not in [the] fear of our God you should walk, because of [the] reproach of the nations our enemies?
pieces: I went on, "What you are doing is not right. Should you not live in the fear of our God, so that the nations who are our enemies have no reason to mock us?

L.9: And I said, "The thing that you are doing is not good. Should you not walk in the fear of our God, because of the reproach of the nations, our enemies?

R.9: I went on, "What you are doing is wrong. You should live in a way that honors our God. Then our enemies from other nations will have no reason to make fun of us.

decisions.choice: and I said
decisions.reason: The written Hebrew has "and he said"; the scribes marked it to be read "and I said", which fits Nehemiah's first-person account. The reading form is followed.

decisions.choice: walk in the fear of our God: live in reverence for God
decisions.reason: "Walk" means to conduct one's life. The fear of God is the reverence that keeps a person from wronging others (Leviticus 25:36, 43, in the laws on lending and debt slavery; Nehemiah 5:15).

decisions.choice: the reproach of the nations: the scorn of the surrounding peoples
decisions.reason: The enemies were already mocking the Jews (3:34-36). If Jews oppressed their own people, it would give the nations more reason to scorn them and their God.

decisions.choice: live in a way that honors our God
decisions.reason: Readable says what "walk in the fear of our God" means in practice.

records.source: וְגַם־אֲנִי֙ אַחַ֣י וּנְעָרַ֔י נֹשִׁ֥ים בָּהֶ֖ם כֶּ֣סֶף וְדָגָ֑ן נַֽעַזְבָה־נָּ֖א אֶת־הַמַּשָּׁ֥א הַזֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: And also I, my brothers and my young men [are] lending to them money and grain; let us abandon, please, this usury.
pieces: I myself, my relatives and my men are also lending them money and grain. Let us stop charging this interest!

L.10: And also I, my brothers and my young men are lending them money and grain. Please, let us give up this [lending at] interest.

R.10: My relatives, my men and I are also lending people money and grain. But let us all stop making them pay interest!

decisions.choice: I too am lending: Nehemiah counts himself among the lenders
decisions.reason: Nehemiah does not condemn lending as such; he too has lent money and grain. What he asks is that all of them give up the burdensome terms.

decisions.choice: this interest: the same practice named in verse 7
decisions.reason: The same word as in verse 7, for loans with interest or pledges.

decisions.choice: my relatives; my men
decisions.reason: As in 4:17, Balanced and Readable say "relatives" and "men" for "brothers" and "young men".

records.source: הָשִׁיבוּ֩ נָ֨א לָהֶ֜ם כְּהַיּ֗וֹם שְׂדֹתֵיהֶ֛ם כַּרְמֵיהֶ֥ם זֵיתֵיהֶ֖ם וּבָתֵּיהֶ֑ם וּמְאַ֨ת הַכֶּ֤סֶף וְהַדָּגָן֙ הַתִּיר֣וֹשׁ וְהַיִּצְהָ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר אַתֶּ֖ם נֹשִׁ֥ים בָּהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: Return, please, to them as the day their fields, their vineyards, their olive groves and their houses, and [the] hundredth of the money and the grain, the new wine and the fresh oil, which you [are] lending to them.
pieces: Give back to them this very day their fields, vineyards, olive groves and houses, and the interest you are charging them on the money, grain, new wine and olive oil."

L.11: Please return to them this very day their fields, their vineyards, their olive groves and their houses, and the hundredth of the money and the grain, the new wine and the oil that you are lending to them."

R.11: Give them back their fields, vineyards, olive groves and houses today! And give back the interest you have charged them on the money, grain, wine and olive oil you lent them."

decisions.choice: as the day: today, at once
decisions.reason: The phrase means "this very day" (1 Samuel 9:13).

decisions.choice: the hundredth: the interest charged, probably one percent a month
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "the hundredth of the money". It most likely means interest of one part in a hundred, charged each month, which comes to twelve percent a year. Some think the word was once "the debt" or "the loan", so that the lenders were to cancel the debts themselves.

decisions.choice: new wine and fresh oil: the farm produce lent to the poor
decisions.reason: Grain, new wine and oil are the main harvest of the land (Deuteronomy 7:13; 14:23). The poor had borrowed food as well as money.

decisions.choice: the interest you are charging (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the most likely sense of "the hundredth" (m2); Literal keeps the word.

records.source: וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ נָשִׁ֗יב וּמֵהֶם֙ לֹ֣א נְבַקֵּ֔שׁ כֵּ֣ן נַעֲשֶׂ֔ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר אַתָּ֣ה אוֹמֵ֑ר וָאֶקְרָא֙ אֶת־הַכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים וָֽאַשְׁבִּיעֵ֔ם לַעֲשׂ֖וֹת כַּדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: And they said, we will return, and from them not we will require; so we will do as you [are] saying. And I called the priests and I made them swear to do according to the word the this.
pieces: They answered, "We will give it back and demand nothing more from them. We will do exactly as you say." Then I called the priests and made the nobles and officials take an oath to do what they had promised.

L.12: And they said, "We will return [it], and we will require nothing from them. We will do just as you say." And I called the priests and made them swear to do according to this word.

R.12: They answered, "We will give it all back. We will not ask them to pay anything more. We will do what you say." Then I called the priests. In front of them I made the leaders promise with an oath to do what they had said.

decisions.choice: we will not require: we will not demand repayment
decisions.reason: The verb means to seek or demand; here, to claim what is owed (Deuteronomy 15:2 speaks of the creditor not pressing his neighbor in the year of release).

decisions.choice: the priests witness an oath
decisions.reason: An oath was sworn in God's name; calling the priests made the promise a solemn act before God and bound the lenders publicly.

decisions.choice: made them swear: the lenders, not the priests
decisions.reason: "Them" refers to the nobles and officials who had just promised. Some read it as the priests, who also lent money; the context of verse 7 points to the lenders.

decisions.choice: the nobles and officials (Balanced); the leaders (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name who swore the oath (m3), which the Hebrew leaves as "them".

records.source: גַּם־חָצְנִ֣י נָעַ֗רְתִּי וָֽאֹמְרָ֡ה כָּ֣כָה יְנַעֵ֪ר הָֽאֱלֹהִ֟ים אֶת־כָּל־הָאִישׁ֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר לֹֽא־יָקִ֜ים אֶת־הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֗ה מִבֵּיתוֹ֙ וּמִ֣יגִיע֔וֹ וְכָ֛כָה יִהְיֶ֥ה נָע֖וּר וָרֵ֑ק וַיֹּאמְר֨וּ כָֽל־הַקָּהָ֜ל אָמֵ֗ן וַֽיְהַלְלוּ֙ אֶת־יְהוָ֔ה וַיַּ֥עַשׂ הָעָ֖ם כַּדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: Also my bosom I shook out, and I said, thus may shake out God every man who not will establish the word the this from his house and from his labor, and thus may he be shaken out and empty. And said all the assembly, Amen, and they praised Yahweh; and did the people according to the word the this.
pieces: I also shook out the fold of my robe and said, "In the same way may God shake out of his house and his property anyone who does not keep this promise. May he be shaken out like this and left with nothing!" The whole assembly said, "Amen," and praised {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. And the people did as they had promised.

L.13: I also shook out the fold of my garment and said, "So may God shake out every man who does not carry out this word, from his house and from his labor, and so may he be shaken out and empty." And all the assembly said, "Amen," and they praised {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. And the people did according to this word.

R.13: Then I shook out the front of my robe. "This is what God will do to anyone who does not keep this promise," I said. "God will shake him out of his house and away from everything he owns, until he has nothing left!" All the people said, "Amen!" and praised {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. And the people did what they had promised.

decisions.choice: shook out the fold of my garment: an acted curse
decisions.reason: The fold of the robe at the chest served as a pocket (Isaiah 49:22; Psalm 129:7). Shaking it out until it was empty showed what God would do to anyone who broke the oath, as prophets acted out their messages (Jeremiah 19:10-11).

decisions.choice: carry out this word ... his labor: keep the promise ... what he has worked for
decisions.reason: The verb means to make a word stand, to keep a promise. "His labor" is what a man has earned by his work, his property (Isaiah 45:14; Psalm 109:11).

decisions.choice: Amen: so be it
decisions.reason: The assembly accepts the curse and binds itself to the oath, as Israel did at the covenant curses (Deuteronomy 27:15-26).

decisions.choice: This is what God will do
decisions.reason: Readable states the curse plainly. The Hebrew is a wish ("may God shake out"); Readable keeps it as a solemn warning in God's name.

records.source: גַּ֞ם מִיּ֣וֹם׀אֲשֶׁר־צִוָּ֣ה אֹתִ֗י לִהְי֣וֹת פֶּחָם֮ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ יְהוּדָה֒ מִשְּׁנַ֣ת עֶשְׂרִ֗ים וְ֠עַד שְׁנַ֨ת שְׁלֹשִׁ֤ים וּשְׁתַּ֨יִם֙ לְאַרְתַּחְשַׁ֣סְתְּא הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ שָׁנִ֖ים שְׁתֵּ֣ים עֶשְׂרֵ֑ה אֲנִ֣י וְאַחַ֔י לֶ֥חֶם הַפֶּ֖חָה לֹ֥א אָכַֽלְתִּי׃
records.gloss: Also from [the] day that he appointed me to be their governor in [the] land of Judah, from [the] year twenty and until [the] year thirty and two of Artaxerxes the king, years two [and] ten, I and my brothers [the] food of the governor not I ate.
pieces: Moreover, from the day I was appointed to be their governor in the land of Judah, from the twentieth year to the thirty-second year of King Artaxerxes, twelve years in all, neither I nor my relatives ate the food allowance of the governor.

L.14: Moreover, from the day that he appointed me to be their governor in the land of Judah, from the twentieth year until the thirty-second year of Artaxerxes the king, twelve years, I and my brothers did not eat the governor's food allowance.

R.14: From the time I was made governor of Judah, my relatives and I never took the food the governor was allowed to collect. That was for twelve years, from the twentieth to the thirty-second year that Artaxerxes was king.

decisions.choice: he appointed me: the king appointed Nehemiah
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "he appointed". The subject is the king named in the same verse.

decisions.choice: the twentieth to the thirty-second year of Artaxerxes: twelve years
decisions.reason: Artaxerxes I ruled Persia from 465 to 424 BC, so these years are about 445 to 433 BC. Nehemiah came in the twentieth year (2:1) and returned to the king in the thirty-second year (13:6).

decisions.choice: the governor's food allowance: provisions paid for by the people
decisions.reason: A governor was entitled to food for his table from taxes on the province (verse 15). Nehemiah refused to take it, so as not to add to the people's burden (verse 18).

decisions.choice: my relatives
decisions.reason: As in 4:17, "my brothers" means Nehemiah's relatives.

records.source: וְהַפַּחוֹת֩ הָרִאשֹׁנִ֨ים אֲשֶׁר־לְפָנַ֜י הִכְבִּ֣ידוּ עַל־הָעָ֗ם וַיִּקְח֨וּ מֵהֶ֜ם בְּלֶ֤חֶם וָיַ֨יִן֙ אַחַר֙ כֶּֽסֶף־שְׁקָלִ֣ים אַרְבָּעִ֔ים גַּ֥ם נַעֲרֵיהֶ֖ם שָׁלְט֣וּ עַל־הָעָ֑ם וַאֲנִי֙ לֹא־עָשִׂ֣יתִי כֵ֔ן מִפְּנֵ֖י יִרְאַ֥ת אֱלֹהִֽים׃
records.gloss: And the governors the former who [were] before me made heavy on the people, and they took from them for food and wine, after silver shekels forty; also their young men domineered over the people; and I not did so because of [the] fear of God.
pieces: The earlier governors before me had laid heavy burdens on the people. They took food and wine from them, as well as {{units:about 1 pound of silver|forty shekels of silver}}. Even their servants lorded it over the people. But I did not act like that, because I feared God.

L.15: But the former governors who [were] before me laid heavy [burdens] on the people and took from them for food and wine, besides forty shekels of silver. Even their young men lorded it over the people. But I did not do so, because of the fear of God.

R.15: The governors before me had made life hard for the people. They demanded food and wine from them, and also {{units:about 1 pound of silver|forty shekels of silver}}. Even their servants bullied the people. But I did not do that, because I respected God.

decisions.choice: besides forty shekels of silver: probably a daily charge on top of the food
alternatives: at the price of forty shekels of silver
decisions.reason: The word "after" here most likely means "besides" or "in addition to". The text does not say how often the forty shekels were taken; a daily charge would have been very heavy, and the context points to a burden that was often repeated.

decisions.choice: the former governors: earlier governors of the province
decisions.reason: Judah had governors before Nehemiah, such as Zerubbabel (Haggai 1:1). The text does not say which governors Nehemiah means.

decisions.choice: because of the fear of God
decisions.reason: Reverence for God kept Nehemiah from using his office to profit at the people's expense; the same reason he urged on the nobles (verse 9).

decisions.choice: servants
decisions.reason: "Young men" here are the governors' attendants and agents; Balanced and Readable say "servants".

decisions.choice: I respected God
decisions.reason: Readable says "respected" for "the fear of God", meaning reverence rather than terror.

records.source: וְ֠גַם בִּמְלֶ֜אכֶת הַחוֹמָ֤ה הַזֹּאת֙ הֶחֱזַ֔קְתִּי וְשָׂדֶ֖ה לֹ֣א קָנִ֑ינוּ וְכָל־נְעָרַ֔י קְבוּצִ֥ים שָׁ֖ם עַל־הַמְּלָאכָֽה׃
records.gloss: And also on [the] work of the wall the this I held fast, and a field not we bought, and all my young men [were] gathered there on the work.
pieces: I devoted myself to the work on this wall, and we did not acquire any land. All my men were gathered there for the work.

L.16: And I also held fast to the work on this wall, and we did not buy any field; and all my young men were gathered there for the work.

R.16: I worked hard on the wall. We did not buy up any land for ourselves. All my men were there working on the wall too.

decisions.choice: held fast: devoted myself, kept at it
decisions.reason: The verb means to be strong or to hold firmly; it is the word used again and again for the builders' work (3:4-32: "repaired", literally "strengthened").

decisions.choice: we did not buy any field: Nehemiah did not profit from the people's debts
decisions.reason: In a famine, land could be bought cheaply from those in debt (verse 3). Nehemiah and his men did not take advantage of this.

decisions.choice: my men
decisions.reason: As in 4:10, "young men" means Nehemiah's own attendants.

records.source: וְהַיְּהוּדִ֨ים וְהַסְּגָנִ֜ים מֵאָ֧ה וַחֲמִשִּׁ֣ים אִ֗ישׁ וְהַבָּאִ֥ים אֵלֵ֛ינוּ מִן־הַגּוֹיִ֥ם אֲשֶׁר־סְבִיבֹתֵ֖ינוּ עַל־שֻׁלְחָנִֽי׃
records.gloss: And the Jews and the officials, hundred and fifty men, and those coming to us from the nations who [were] around us, [were] at my table.
pieces: Besides, 150 Jews and officials ate at my table, as well as those who came to us from the surrounding nations.

L.17: And the Jews and the officials, 150 men, and those who came to us from the nations that [were] around us, [were] at my table.

R.17: Every day 150 Jews and officials ate at my table. So did visitors who came to us from other nations around us.

decisions.choice: 150 men at the governor's table
decisions.reason: A governor was expected to host officials and guests. Nehemiah fed them at his own cost (verse 18).

decisions.choice: those who came from the nations around us: visitors from neighboring peoples
decisions.reason: These were foreign envoys or traders, or Jews returning from other lands, who were guests of the governor.

decisions.choice: Every day
decisions.reason: Readable adds "every day", which verse 18 makes clear.

records.source: וַאֲשֶׁר֩ הָיָ֨ה נַעֲשֶׂ֜ה לְי֣וֹם אֶחָ֗ד שׁ֣וֹר אֶחָ֞ד צֹ֠אן שֵׁשׁ־בְּרֻר֤וֹת וְצִפֳּרִים֙ נַֽעֲשׂוּ־לִ֔י וּבֵ֨ין עֲשֶׂ֧רֶת יָמִ֛ים בְּכָל־יַ֖יִן לְהַרְבֵּ֑ה וְעִם־זֶ֗ה לֶ֤חֶם הַפֶּחָה֙ לֹ֣א בִקַּ֔שְׁתִּי כִּֽי־כָֽבְדָ֥ה הָעֲבֹדָ֖ה עַל־הָעָ֥ם הַזֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: And what was prepared for one day [was] one ox, sheep six choice ones, and birds were prepared for me, and once in ten days all [kinds of] wine in abundance; and with this [the] food of the governor not I sought, because was heavy the service on the people the this.
pieces: Each day one ox, six choice sheep and some birds were prepared for me, and every ten days a large supply of all kinds of wine. In spite of all this, I never demanded the governor's food allowance, because the people already carried a heavy burden.

L.18: And what was prepared for one day was one ox [and] six choice sheep, and birds were prepared for me; and every ten days all [kinds of] wine in abundance. Yet with all this I did not demand the governor's food allowance, because the service was heavy on this people.

R.18: Each day we prepared one ox, six of the best sheep and some birds. Every ten days we brought in plenty of wine of every kind. Even so, I never asked for the food the governor was allowed to collect, because the people were already working so hard.

decisions.choice: one ox, six choice sheep and birds a day: food for a large household
decisions.reason: The meat was enough to feed the 150 men of verse 17 and the guests. Nehemiah paid for it himself.

decisions.choice: every ten days: wine was supplied once each ten days
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "between ten days", meaning at intervals of ten days.

decisions.choice: the service was heavy: the burden of labor and tax
decisions.reason: The word means work or service. It covers the forced labor of building and the taxes the people already paid to the king (verse 4).

records.source: זָכְרָה־לִּ֥י אֱלֹהַ֖י לְטוֹבָ֑ה כֹּ֥ל אֲשֶׁר־עָשִׂ֖יתִי עַל־הָעָ֥ם הַזֶּֽה׃פ
records.gloss: Remember for me, my God, for good, all that I have done for the people the this.
pieces: Remember me, my God, for good, for all that I have done for this people.

L.19: Remember for me, my God, for good, all that I have done for this people.

R.19: My God, remember me and be good to me because of all I have done for these people.

decisions.choice: remember me for good: a short prayer in the memoir
decisions.reason: Nehemiah's account is broken by short prayers like this one (6:14; 13:14, 22, 29, 31). He asks God to take note of what he has done and to deal kindly with him; he does not claim to have earned a reward.

decisions.choice: for this people: on behalf of this people
decisions.reason: The preposition here means "on behalf of": what Nehemiah did for the people's good (verses 14-18).

decisions.choice: Remember for me ... for good (Literal); Remember me ... for good (Balanced); remember me and be good to me (Readable)
decisions.reason: The book-wide wording for this prayer (13:14, 22, 31).
